fullPassage:
Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide, commonly referred to as CO2. This gas itself is not dangerous when we encounter it in everyday situations. However, excessive amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, resulting in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously threatening life on our planet. We must act immediately to stop any further climate change.

While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting solutions available. In this report, we will focus on one of the most powerful nature-based solutions to climate change: whales, the giant helpers living under the sea.

Whales are amazing creatures. They are enormous and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh over 200 tons, and some whales have been known to live for more than 100 years. These giants do extremely beneficial things for the environment throughout their long lives and even after death. According to scientists, a single whale can absorb about 550 kilograms of CO2 per year, while a tree can absorb only 22.

Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean floor with all the CO2 they absorbed during their lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats for deep-sea creatures. This process is called a whale fall. Whale falls permanently bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year. This achievement is basically what expensive carbon capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon and then store it underground.

In addition to their direct absorption and burial of CO2 through whale falls, whales also make a significant indirect contribution to reducing CO2 through an act called a whale pump. This refers to the vertical movements of whales that help circulate nutrients across different depths of the ocean. Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface to breathe. When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is rich in nutrients that are essential for creatures living in that area. Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the ocean.

These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. They do this through photosynthesis, a process that creates energy using carbon, water, and light. It is estimated that increasing the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees. Whale pumps deliver nutrients not only to the ocean surface but also to deeper areas of the ocean. As whales swim back down to feed at the ocean's bottom, their movements stir up the water and bring nutrients down to the creatures living below. Whale pumps promote the growth of marine life at various depths throughout the ocean.

Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also horizontally through a process called the great whale conveyor belt. These giant mammals migrate over long distances at certain times of the year. For example, in the summer, humpback whales tend to stay near Alaska, where the water is cold but rich in nutrients and prey for them to feed on. As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii.

Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. Fortunately, when the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters. These nutrients support the life of many marine animals and, importantly, encourage the growth of phytoplankton even in warm waters. The spread of phytoplankton leads to increased carbon absorption throughout the entire ocean. Whales circulate water and nutrients to every corner of the ocean, helping to combat climate change.

Despite the important roles of whales in our environment, their lives are at serious risk. The number of whales had dramatically dropped until killing them for commercial purposes was officially banned in 1986. It is estimated that the global whale population fell from 4 to 5 million to just over 1 million during the decades before the ban. Today, whales are still threatened by various man-made dangers, such as fishing nets, ship strikes, and microplastic pollution in the ocean. It is important to recognize that whales are valuable partners in our fight against the climate crisis and that protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge. Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.

questions.passage: Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide, commonly ①<u>referred</u> to as CO2. This gas itself is not dangerous when we encounter it in everyday situations. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously ③<u>threatening</u> life on our planet. We must act immediately ④<u>stop</u> any further climate change.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'to stop'인데 to가 빠져 있다. act + to부정사(목적) 구문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① referred: 과거분사 (commonly referred to as = ~로 불리는)
✅ ② resulting: 분사구문 (결과를 나타냄)
✅ ③ threatening: 현재분사 (is threatening = 위협하고 있다)
❌ ④ stop → to stop: act immediately to stop (목적의 to부정사)
det.tip: act + to V: ~하기 위해 행동하다. to 없이 stop만 쓰면 비문.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'only 22'인데 'one'으로 바뀌었다. only(단지)가 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① weigh: 병렬 구조 (can grow and weigh)
✅ ② to live: be known to V (~하는 것으로 알려지다)
✅ ③ beneficial: 형용사 (extremely beneficial things)
❌ ④ one → only: 'a tree can absorb only 22' 부사 only(단지)
det.tip: only = 부사(단지, 겨우). one = 수사/대명사. 550 vs 22 대비를 강조하는 only가 필요.

questions.passage: In addition to their direct absorption and burial of CO2 through whale falls, whales also make a significant indirect contribution to ①<u>reducing</u> CO2 through an act called a whale pump. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'to breathe'인데 'breathing'으로 바뀌었다. 목적의 to부정사가 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reducing: 전치사 to + 동명사 (contribution to reducing)
✅ ② circulate: help + 동사원형 (help circulate)
❌ ③ breathing → to breathe: swim up to the surface to breathe (목적의 to부정사)
✅ ④ rich: 형용사 후치수식 (waste rich in nutrients)
det.tip: to breathe: 숨을 쉬기 위해(목적). help + V원형: help circulate (O).

questions.passage: These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when ①<u>taken</u> together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. It is estimated that ③<u>increasing</u> the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to ④<u>plant</u> 2 billion new trees.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 'be equivalent to + V-ing'에서 to는 전치사이므로 동명사 planting이 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① taken: 분사구문 (when taken together = 함께 고려하면)
✅ ② creates: 주격 관계대명사절 동사 (a process that creates)
✅ ③ increasing: 가주어-진주어 (It is estimated that increasing... is)
❌ ④ plant → planting: be equivalent to -ing (to = 전치사)
det.tip: be equivalent to + -ing: ~에 해당하다. 이때 to는 전치사. look forward to -ing과 같은 구조.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'under the sea(바다 속)'인데 'ground(땅)'로 바뀌었다. 고래는 바다에 산다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① excessive(과도한): 원문 일치
✅ ② economical(경제적인): 원문 일치
❌ ③ ground(땅) → sea(바다): 고래는 바다 밑에 사는 동물
✅ ④ immediately(즉시): 원문 일치

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'essential(필수적인)'인데 'harmful(해로운)'로 바뀌었다. 영양분은 생물에게 필수적이지 해롭지 않다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① permanently(영구적으로): 원문 일치
✅ ② capture(포획하다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ reducing(줄이는): 원문 일치
❌ ④ harmful(해로운) → essential(필수적인): 영양분이 생물에게 필수적
det.tip: essential(필수적인) ↔ harmful(해로운). 영양분은 생물에게 essential.

questions.passage: Whales are amazing creatures. They are enormous and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh over 200 tons, and some whales have been known to live for more than 100 years. questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"나무 한 그루가 고래 한 마리보다 더 많은 CO2를 흡수한다."

det.korean: F. 원문: 고래 한 마리 = 550kg CO2/년, 나무 한 그루 = 22kg CO2/년. 고래가 훨씬 더 많이 흡수한다.
det.analysis: 고래 550kg vs 나무 22kg → 고래가 약 25배 더 많이 흡수. 진술문은 정반대이므로 F.
det.tip: 수치 비교: 550 >> 22. '나무가 더 많이'는 거짓.

questions.passage: Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean floor with all the CO2 they absorbed during their lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats for deep-sea creatures. questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"고래 낙하(whale fall)는 매년 약 145,000톤의 CO2를 영구적으로 바다 속에 묻는다."

det.korean: T. 원문: 'Whale falls permanently bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year.' 정확히 일치.
det.analysis: 진술문과 원문 내용이 완전히 일치한다. 수치(145,000톤)와 '영구적으로' 모두 정확.
det.tip: permanently = 영구적으로. 숫자 정확히 확인: 145,000톤/년.

questions.passage: Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also horizontally through a process called the great whale conveyor belt. These giant mammals migrate over long distances at certain times of the year. questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"혹등고래는 여름에 하와이 근처의 따뜻한 바다에 머문다."

det.korean: F. 원문: 여름에는 알래스카 근처에 머물고, 겨울이 다가오면 하와이로 이동한다. 계절이 반대.
det.analysis: summer → Alaska (차갑지만 영양분 풍부), winter → Hawaii (따뜻한 물, 번식). 진술문은 계절 뒤바뀜. F.
det.tip: humpback whales: summer=Alaska, winter=Hawaii. 계절-장소 매칭에 주의.

questions.passage: However, excessive amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, resulting in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. We must act immediately to stop any further climate change. While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting solutions available. In this report, we will focus on one of the most powerful __________ solutions to climate change: whales, the giant helpers living under the sea.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고래는 자연 기반(nature-based) 해결책이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ nature-based: 원문 일치. 고기술(high-tech) 대안으로 자연 기반 제시
❌ ① technology-based: 앞 문장에서 high-tech은 비싸다고 함
❌ ② government-funded: 정부 지원 언급 없음
❌ ④ industry-driven: 산업 주도 언급 없음
det.tip: high-tech(비싸고 제한적) ↔ nature-based(경제적이고 오래 지속). 대조 구조.

questions.passage: Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. Fortunately, when the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters. These nutrients support the life of many marine animals and, importantly, encourage the growth of phytoplankton even in warm waters. The spread of phytoplankton leads to increased __________ throughout the entire ocean.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 식물성 플랑크톤의 확산은 전체 바다에서 탄소 흡수(carbon absorption) 증가로 이어진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① carbon absorption: 원문 일치. 식물성 플랑크톤 = CO2 흡수 역할
❌ ② water temperature: 수온 상승은 글의 문제이지 결과 아님
❌ ③ whale migration: 이동은 원인이지 결과 아님
❌ ④ nutrient scarcity: 영양분 부족이 아니라 영양분 공급이 핵심
det.tip: phytoplankton → carbon absorption(탄소 흡수). 글의 핵심 논리 흐름.

questions.passage: In addition to their direct absorption and burial of CO2 through whale falls, whales also make a significant indirect contribution to reducing CO2 through an act called a whale pump. This refers to the vertical movements of whales that help circulate nutrients across different depths of the ocean. Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface to breathe. When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 고래 펌프는 CO2를 직접 흡수하는 과정을 말한다.
고래는 해수면에서 먹이를 먹고 깊은 바다로 숨을 쉬러 간다.
고래의 수평적 이동이 고래 펌프의 핵심이다.
고래가 수면 근처에서 막대한 양의 배설물을 배출한다.

det.korean: ④ 원문: 'When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste.' 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 수면 근처에서 막대한 양의 폐기물 방출: 원문 일치
❌ ① 직접 흡수가 아니라 'indirect contribution(간접 기여)'
❌ ② 깊은 바다에서 먹이를 먹고 수면으로 숨을 쉬러 감 (반대)
❌ ③ 수직적(vertical) 이동이 핵심, 수평적 아님
det.tip: whale pump = 수직 이동(vertical movements). 직접(direct) ↔ 간접(indirect).

questions.passage: Despite the important roles of whales in our environment, their lives are at serious risk. The number of whales had dramatically dropped until killing them for commercial purposes was officially banned in 1986. It is estimated that the global whale population fell from 4 to 5 million to just over 1 million during the decades before the ban. Today, whales are still threatened by various man-made dangers, such as fishing nets, ship strikes, and microplastic pollution in the ocean.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 상업 목적의 고래 포획은 1986년에 공식적으로 금지되었다.
포획 금지 이후 고래 개체수가 400~500만 마리로 회복되었다.
현재 고래는 어망, 선박 충돌 등 인위적 위험에 처해 있다.
금지 이전 수십 년간 전 세계 고래 개체수가 급감했다.

det.korean: ② 원문: 400~500만에서 100만 조금 넘는 수로 감소한 것이지, 회복된 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② 4~5 million → just over 1 million은 '감소'이며, 금지 이전의 수치. 회복 언급 없음
✅ ① 1986년 금지: 원문 일치
✅ ③ fishing nets, ship strikes, microplastic: 원문 일치
✅ ④ dramatically dropped during decades before the ban: 원문 일치
det.tip: fell from 4~5 million to 1 million = 감소. 회복(recovery)이 아닌 감소(decline).

questions.passage: (a) These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant. (b) But when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. (c) They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. (d) It is estimated that increasing the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to plant 2 billion new trees.
questions.stem: 위 (a)~(d) 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?

det.korean: (d) 'equivalent to plant' → 'equivalent to planting': be equivalent to에서 to는 전치사이므로 동명사 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ (a) called phytoplankton: 과거분사 삽입구 정상
✅ (b) when taken together: 분사구문 정상
✅ (c) absorb and produce: 병렬 구조 정상
❌ (d) to plant → to planting: be equivalent to + -ing (to = 전치사)
det.tip: be equivalent to + V-ing: ~에 해당하다. equivalent to planting (O), equivalent to plant (X).

questions.passage: Whales are amazing creatures. They are enormous and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh over 200 tons, and some whales have been known to live for more than 100 years. These giants do extremely beneficial things for the environment throughout their long lives and even after death.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"이 거대한 동물들은 긴 생애 동안 그리고 죽은 이후에도 환경에 매우 (          )한 일들을 한다."

det.korean: 원문: 'do extremely beneficial things for the environment'
det.analysis: 원문에서 beneficial(유익한)이 환경에 대한 기여를 설명. extremely beneficial things.
det.tip: beneficial = 유익한, 이로운. 환경에 beneficial한 일들을 한다.

questions.passage: It is important to recognize that whales are valuable partners in our fight against the climate crisis and that protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge. Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"고래를 보호하는 것은 이 세계적 도전을 해결하는 효과적이고 비용 (          )인 방법이다."

det.korean: 원문: 'an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge'
det.analysis: cost-efficient = 비용 효율적인. 빈칸은 '비용 ___'이므로 efficient가 답.
det.tip: cost-efficient = 비용 효율적인. effective(효과적인)와 함께 고래 보호의 장점.

questions.passage: Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the ocean. These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, __________.
questions.stem:
주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)
[ they / play / a / significant / role / in / reducing / CO2 ]
questions.wa: they play a significant role in reducing CO2
accept: they play a significant role in reducing CO2
They play a significant role in reducing CO2
they play a significant role in reducing CO2.
They play a significant role in reducing CO2.

det.korean: 그것들은 CO2를 줄이는 데 중요한 역할을 한다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'they play a significant role in reducing CO2.' 8단어 배열.
det.tip: play a role in + -ing: ~하는 데 역할을 하다. in은 전치사 → 뒤에 동명사.

questions.passage: Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide. While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting solutions available. In this report, we will focus on one of the most powerful nature-based solutions to climate change: whales, the giant helpers living under the sea.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 고기술 탄소 포집 기술의 최신 발전 동향
기후 변화에 대한 자연 기반 해결책으로서의 고래의 역할
지난 200년간 인간 활동이 환경에 미친 부정적 영향
이산화탄소 배출을 줄이기 위한 국제 협약의 중요성

det.korean: 글의 주제: 기후 변화에 대한 자연 기반 해결책으로서 고래의 역할.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 본문 전체의 핵심: 고래 = nature-based solution to climate change
❌ ① 고기술은 비싸다고 언급만 함
❌ ③ 도입부 배경일 뿐
❌ ④ 국제 협약 언급 없음
det.tip: 도입부에서 문제 제기(CO2) → 해결책(고래) 전개. 핵심 키워드: nature-based solution.

questions.passage: Despite the important roles of whales in our environment, their lives are at serious risk. The number of whales had dramatically dropped until killing them for commercial purposes was officially banned in 1986. It is estimated that the global whale population fell from 4 to 5 million to just over 1 million during the decades before the ban. Today, whales are still threatened by various man-made dangers, such as fishing nets, ship strikes, and microplastic pollution in the ocean. It is important to recognize that whales are valuable partners in our fight against the climate crisis and that protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 고래 개체수가 이미 충분히 회복되었으므로 더 이상 보호가 필요하지 않다.
기후 변화는 고래와 무관한 문제이므로 기술적 해결이 유일한 방법이다.
고래 포획 금지 이후 인위적 위험 요소가 완전히 제거되었다.
고래를 보호하는 것이 기후 위기에 대응하는 효과적이고 경제적인 방법이다.

det.korean: 요지: 고래를 보호하는 것이 기후 위기 대응의 효과적이고 경제적인 방법이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 원문 마지막 문장: 'protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way'
❌ ① 아직 위험에 처해 있다고 명시
❌ ② 고래가 핵심 해결책이라는 것이 글의 주장
❌ ③ 여전히 fishing nets, ship strikes 등 위협 받고 있음
det.tip: 결론부의 핵심: valuable partners, effective and cost-efficient. 보호 필요성 강조.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
"기후 변화를 막기 위해 더 많은 고래가 더 오래 건강하게 살도록 도와주자."
[조건] take action / help / live 를 사용할 것
questions.wa: Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.
accept: Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.
Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives
let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives
Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives!

det.korean: 더 많은 고래가 더 오래 건강하게 살도록 행동에 나서자.
det.analysis: take action to V: ~하기 위해 행동하다. help + O + V원형: ~가 ~하도록 돕다. live longer and healthier lives.
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형: help whales live (O). take action to V: 행동에 나서다.
